display.purpose: Home-page lead and rare identity-scale statements.

headline.purpose: Major public sections and detail headings.

title.purpose: Service rubrics and compact editorial headings.

body.purpose: Instructions, facts, caveats, and operational content.

label.purpose: Visible labels, navigation, actions, and metadata.

brand.purpose: Wordmarks from 1.1rem to 1.35rem and rare identity labels from .62rem to .72rem.

shadows.name: editorial-photo-lift
shadows.purpose: Documentary photographs in the migrated home collage only.

shadows.name: inherited-working-instrument
shadows.purpose: Legacy private or administrative dark work surfaces only; never an ordinary public container.

shadows.name: featured-provider-sheet
shadows.purpose: The single approved-provider search result only; never repeated on ONRC rows.

motion.name: editorial-seal-turn
motion.purpose: Slow identity rotation on the home collage seal; disabled for reduced motion.

motion.name: editorial-tool-breathe
motion.purpose: Small wrench motion inside the home wordmark; disabled for reduced motion.

motion.name: editorial-state
motion.purpose: Interaction-triggered field focus underline, search-button arrow/lift, and category underline/icon/arrow feedback only; reduced motion collapses transitions to effectively instant durations.

motion.name: home-headline-arrive
motion.purpose: Home headline only: a single 18px vertical transform into place, with no opacity change.

motion.name: home-search-rule-arrive
motion.purpose: The home search instrument's brick top rule expands from the left once, closing the entrance sequence.

motion.name: reduced-motion-final-state
motion.purpose: Remove home entrance animations, render the headline and search rule in their final state, and collapse interaction-feedback transition durations while preserving focus indication.

motion.name: provider-route-sequence
motion.purpose: Public provider profile only: house draws, service route follows, then the identity title resolves. Reduced motion makes the sequence effectively instant.

narrative.overview:
ServiciiAproape is one warm contemporary local edition across public, customer, provider and administrative surfaces: uncoated paper, deep editorial ink, decisive coral, lavender identity marks, mint working states and documentary photographs of tradespeople in action. Information density changes with the task, but the product no longer switches visual worlds between discovery and operations.

The home opening remains deliberately asymmetric: a compressed promise and three-step locality search sit beside an overlapping photographic collage. Elsewhere, ruled navigation, clean-paper work sheets and compact ledgers preserve the same editorial rhythm without compromising operational clarity. Search semantics, ONRC caveats, language behavior and every authorization boundary remain unchanged.

Motion belongs to identity and direct feedback: a slow seal turn, a restrained wrench breath and a short button lift. Reduced motion freezes identity animation while preserving the complete composition and visible focus.

Final design review verdict: SHIP.
keyCharacteristics: Warm editorial ground, deep ink, coral action, lavender identity and mint working states across the product.
Nimbus Narrow Local for compressed display hierarchy; Carlito Local for body copy, controls and labels.
An asymmetric documentary trade collage paired with a numbered county → locality → service search.
One animated house-and-wrench identity reused in every masthead and the admin shell, static for reduced motion.
Flat search rows, ruled workspace navigation and compact ledgers rather than generic card stacks.
Truthful distinctions between ONRC facts, provider declarations, administrative review, internal preview and public visibility.
One visual system across catalogue, provider profile, customer portal, provider workspace and administration.

rules.name: The Coral-Is-The-Primary-Action Rule
rules.body: Coral belongs to primary actions, step numbers and small registration marks across the product; it never becomes a section wash.

rules.name: The Collage-Owns-Depth Rule
rules.body: Only documentary photographs carry lift on the migrated home; navigation, search and service rubrics stay flat.

rules.name: The Living-Seal Rule
rules.body: Identity motion belongs to the slow seal and subtle logo-tool breath; explanatory copy and documentary photographs remain still.

rules.name: The Brick-Is-An-Action Rule
rules.body: Muted brick belongs to the primary action, focus, selection, icons, and small editorial punctuation; it does not become a large decorative wash.

rules.name: The Paper-Stays-Warm Rule
rules.body: Default reading surfaces remain warm paper. Clean paper is a controlled interaction lift, not a replacement page background.

rules.name: The Truth-Needs-Words Rule
rules.body: Sage, brick, and red can accelerate scanning, but status copy must name what is declared, reviewed, blocked, previewed, or public.

rules.name: The Serif-Leads Rule
rules.body: Serif establishes editorial hierarchy; controls, labels, long copy, dense facts, and administrative work stay in Carlito.

rules.name: The Locality-First Rule
rules.body: Preserve the visible county → locality dependency and the complete primary action before supporting explanation at every viewport.

rules.name: The Six–Three–Two Rule
rules.body: The six service rubrics render six across on desktop, three on tablet, and two on phone; do not collapse them into a generic one-column card feed.

rules.name: The One-Lift Rule
rules.body: Public surfaces stay flat at rest except for the single approved-provider search sheet. Use rules, paper tone, and whitespace for every ordinary ONRC row; never repeat the shadow into a card feed.

rules.name: The Square-Page Rule
rules.body: Warmth comes from paper, serif type, color, and spacing—not rounded cards or pill controls.

rules.name: The One-Hand Rule
rules.body: All field and category icons should look drawn by one hand: consistent stroke weight, no emoji, no icon-font substitutions, and no decorative filled badges.

rules.name: The County-Owns-Locality Rule
rules.body: Never show locality as independent free text or retain choices from a previous county. Loading, empty, failure, and no-JavaScript states keep the visible county → locality sequence.

rules.name: The Restrained-Home-Motion Rule
rules.body: Home motion is limited to headline transform → one-time search top rule, then local field, button, and category feedback. Do not animate the location note, process text, or any route graph.

rules.name: The Legal-Identity-Before-Account Rule
rules.body: Registration confirms a mailbox and opens staff verification; it never visually or verbally collapses legal reconciliation, claim review, account activation, profile creation, or publication into one success state.

rules.name: The Workflow-Inherits-Color-Not-Authority Rule
rules.body: A shared palette never merges public registry facts, provider declarations, staff decisions, private drafts, credentials, or publication state.

rules.name: The Featured-Sheet-Is-Not-A-Ranking Rule
rules.body: The single approved-provider fact sheet distinguishes a richer provider-supplied publication snapshot from compact ONRC facts; its prominence never means recommendation, ranking, quality, or guaranteed availability.

rules.name: The Route-Then-Facts Rule
rules.body: Use one house-to-service drawing to orient the visitor, then close the opening with the exact service, searched locality and availability ledger; do not introduce a second competing hero effect.

rules.name: The Contact-Is-A-Declaration Rule
rules.body: Contact and availability remain explicitly provider-supplied even when they are visually prominent and part of an approved snapshot.

rules.name: The Project-Is-Not-A-Delivery Rule
rules.body: Count demand once per customer project; show provider deliveries separately so multi-provider dispatch never inflates locality demand.

rules.name: The Policy-Is-Not-Taxonomy Rule
rules.body: Operational category controls may change discovery, new-provider intake, and order, but never imply that they edit CAEN facts, existing provider services, or immutable publication history.

dos: Do keep the public canvas warm, flat, and editorial, with generous whitespace and ruled structure.
Do use Noto Serif Local for editorial display and Carlito Local for controls, body copy, metadata, and administration.
Do make locality search the first complete instrument and keep county ownership of SIRUTA locality choices visible.
Do pair the desktop home headline with one restrained editorial location note, then hide that note on phone so search appears by roughly 456px.
Do limit home motion to the headline transform, one-time search top rule, field focus underline, search-button arrow/lift, and category underline/icon/arrow feedback.
Do render service categories as six ruled rubrics, three on tablet and two on phone.
Do use custom consistent-stroke SVGs for fields and categories, with one visual hand across the set.
Do keep the primary action muted brick and retain strong focus outlines, labels, touch targets, and reduced motion.
Do keep ONRC source dates, registered-office wording, licenses, and caveats adjacent to catalogue results.
Do feature one approved provider as a square-edged clean-paper fact sheet with `210px × 190px` cover media on desktop, `16:9` media on phone, three declared fact groups, and one `44px` CTA.
Do keep ordinary ONRC results as compact ruled rows that remain scannable and pageable at hundreds of records.
Do keep the public provider profile's identity, drawn route and three declared facts together in the opening sequence.
Do keep phone, e-mail, website, professional address, availability, coverage and portfolio provenance explicitly provider-supplied wherever present.
Do keep missing-company registration form-first on phones and keep the no-account/no-publication boundary adjacent to the form and confirmation result.
Do distinguish provider-supplied facts, review, private draft, internal preview, visibility, withdrawal, and failure in words.
Do preserve existing claim, activation, profile, moderation, publication, password, and administrative authorization boundaries.
donts: Don't add gradients, glass effects, heavy dark panels, decorative blobs, or floating card grids to the public journal.
Don't add rounded cards, pill buttons, or unrelated icon styles.
Don't use brick as a broad wash or sage as a trust badge.
Don't replace the ruled locality instrument with a generic hero card or bury it below promotional copy.
Don't restore the rejected home route graph, animate static process text, add a competing entrance effect, or fade the home headline.
Don't turn service rubrics into rounded cards or collapse the phone grid to one column.
Don't imply ONRC registration proves coverage, availability, competence, quality, or recommendation.
Don't repeat the featured provider shadow, media treatment, or CTA block across ONRC results, and don't present the featured sheet as ranking or endorsement.
Don't show the internal-preview badge unless the provider result is actually in internal preview.
Don't let the provider profile's prominent contact action or administrative-review copy imply endorsement, current capacity, response time or acceptance of work.
Don't present missing-company registration as account creation, self-publication, or a shortcut around legal reconciliation and claim review.
Don't let shared visuals blur mailbox control, legal representation, private editing, administrative approval, or publication.
Don't hide caveats, field errors, disabled dependencies, or fail-closed states for visual neatness.
